rows.context: Interprets slavery through class, culture and paternalism as contested domination. His preface’s national-culture framing and later criticism remain visible; paternalism is not a claim of benign slavery.
rows.works: Roll, Jordan, Roll (1974), preface, acknowledgments and opening paternalism discussion

existing_sources_reused.title: Eugene D. Genovese, Roll, Jordan, Roll: The World the Slaves Made (Pantheon, 1974).
existing_sources_reused.citation: Eugene D. Genovese, Roll, Jordan, Roll: The World the Slaves Made (Pantheon, 1974).

verification.note: Read original-publication statement (Pantheon 1974; Vintage 1976), complete preface dated August 1973 and acknowledgments, and initial On Paternalism paragraphs in the 2011 ebook preview. Class/nationality and paternalism are his contested interpretation. Acknowledgments explicitly credit Rawick, Levine, Litwack, Fogel/Engerman and Elizabeth Fox-Genovese; these do not establish coauthorship or agreement. No complete book or direct Gramsci passage read. White-transcribed dialect and master/slave analogies are not independently validated.

existing_sources_reused.title: Walter Johnson, “A Nettlesome Classic Turns Twenty-Five,” Commonplace 1.4 (July 2001), retrospective review of Genovese.
existing_sources_reused.citation: Walter Johnson, “A Nettlesome Classic Turns Twenty-Five,” Commonplace 1.4 (July 2001), retrospective review of Genovese.

verification.note: Complete review read through overlapping web/local extracts. Attributes a Gramscian interpretation and contests paternalism/consent, foregrounding coercion and sale. Johnson’s criticism is an interpretation, not unanimous judgment. The retrospective 2001 source does not extend mapped coverage beyond 2000 or replace an original Genovese Gramsci passage; site modification dates are not publication dates.

reading_limit: Existing primary preface/opening and named Johnson reading retain all qualifications. Earlier/later political identities do not collapse the writings into one timeless position. Levin is a named substantive reader, not Genovese’s own statement. No direct Gramsci passage has been checked, and acknowledgments do not establish agreement or coauthorship.

relations.relationship: Interprets enslaved culture and paternalism as contested forms within a system of domination.
relations.evidence_note: Existing complete preface and initial paternalism paragraphs, plus Walter Johnson’s complete retrospective, within their recorded scopes. Paternalism is not a benign-slavery claim; Johnson’s consent/coercion criticism remains visible.

relations.relationship: Makes the relation between slaveholding class power, economic organization and development a problem for Marxist historical interpretation.
relations.evidence_note: Specific political-economy intervention mediated by N. Gordon Levin’s substantive review, selected opening pages. This is a contribution to a contested interpretation, not proof that every Marxist shared it, or a direct personal influence from Marx or Gramsci.
